timeline.text: Chest x-ray: right lower lobe opacity
Chest x-ray: pulmonary vascular congestion, small bilateral effusions

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 48-year-old female admitted for community-acquired pneumonia. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.51, bnp 915, creatinine 1.02, hemoglobin 12.1, platelets 315, sodium 139, wbc 8.2; vitals dbp 64-70, heart_rate 81-85, map 87-92, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 132-136, spo2 97-99, temp 36.9-37.1
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Chest x-ray: pulmonary vascular congestion, small bilateral effusions; Chest x-ray: right lower lobe opacity; Furosemide 40 mg IV; Transthoracic echo: LVEF 30%, global hypokinesis
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia. Acute systolic heart failure.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.03, hemoglobin 12, platelets 312, sodium 139, wbc 8.3; vitals dbp 65-69, heart_rate 80-85, map 88-92, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 131-138, spo2 97-98, temp 36.9-37.2
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Furosemide 40 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia. Acute systolic heart failure. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 48-year-old female, length of stay 5 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Community-acquired pneumonia. Acute systolic heart failure. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
